clue.text: Whimsically Cain became one east of Eden escorting stranger

indicators.note: east is the right-hand side on a map, so the east end of a word is its final letter

parts.note: the eastern, final letter of Eden
stranger as in more odd

explanation.surface: A Bible-study musing on Cain's fate after being exiled east of Eden with some outsider.
explanation.walkthrough: Genesis sends Cain to the land of Nod, east of Eden, so whimsically he became a dweller of Nod. The N escorts, or goes before, the comparative.
explanation.definitionFit: A playful coinage: a resident of the land of Nod would be a 'Nodder', and the real word means a person who nods.

clue.text: When pigs fly? Sure enough about grasping it

indicators.note: about here means turned round, so the held letters run from right to left
the phrase is said to hold the word inside itself, across the gap between two words

parts.note: letters running across the two words, from the end of the first into the second

explanation.surface: A sceptic's retort: when pigs fly? and someone answering that it is sure enough.
explanation.walkthrough: NE'ER is the poetic contraction of never; the grid ignores the apostrophe.
explanation.definitionFit: 'When pigs fly' is an idiom for something that will never happen, so the poetic contraction of never fits.

clue.text: Rarely any woe with Cain involved

indicators.note: involved means tangled up together, so these letters are mixed into a new order

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: Rarely does any misery come to someone who has Cain mixed up in it, which is ironic given Cain's story.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase means occasionally or only now and then, a synonym of seldom.

clue.text: Doyens in court watchers wanting one date

indicators.note: wanting means lacking, so a single letter is missing from the watchers' word

parts.note: in real tennis the dedans is the spectators' gallery, and by extension the spectators themselves
D is the abbreviation for date

explanation.surface: Senior figures sitting among the watchers at a court case, but missing one appointment.
explanation.walkthrough: Real tennis, the old indoor game, has a gallery behind the service end called the dedans; one of its two Ds goes.
explanation.definitionFit: A dean, as in the dean of a diplomatic corps, is its senior member, much as a doyen is.

clue.text: Right off ruddy fodder

indicators.note: off means removed, so the letter for right is taken away from the colour word

parts.note: ruddy means of a reddish colour
R is the standard abbreviation for right

explanation.surface: A farmer complaining that the wretched animal feed has gone off.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Ruddy' reads as a mild British swear word, but it is the colour.
explanation.definitionFit: Eddish is a dialect word for aftermath, the second growth of grass after mowing, used as cattle feed.

clue.text: Somerset's channel blowing the lid on gullible — one looking up

indicators.note: blowing off the lid removes the top, and in a down light the top is the first letter

parts.note: green means naive and easily fooled
surface padding: a wink at 1 down, which is this answer read upwards

explanation.surface: Exposing someone gullible in Somerset while one person gazes skywards.
explanation.walkthrough: 'One looking up' is a playful nod to 1 down: this answer read upwards is that answer. Somerset is a county in south-west England.
explanation.definitionFit: A reen (or rhine) is a drainage ditch on the Somerset Levels, a regional word for a channel.

clue.text: Songs about diminished county

parts.note: C for circa, Latin for about
Hants is the shortened form of Hampshire, an English county

explanation.surface: Music celebrating a county that has shrunk in size.
explanation.definitionFit: Chants are songs, especially repetitive ones sung in worship or by football crowds.

clue.text: Shut up! Abbess invested in that stole from old Savile Row

indicators.note: to invest is to clothe or surround, so the religious head is wrapped inside the other word

parts.note: shut up as in confined
ABB is an abbreviation for abbess

explanation.surface: An abbess wearing a fashionable stole from a Savile Row tailor is told to be quiet.
explanation.walkthrough: Savile Row is London's street of bespoke tailors; 'stole' looks like a scarf but is a past-tense verb.
explanation.definitionFit: Cabbage was old tailors' slang for offcuts of cloth kept on the sly, and to cabbage was to pilfer them.

clue.text: Goal confines one playing

parts.note: an ambit is a boundary or scope
Roman numeral one
on, as an actor is on stage

explanation.surface: A football goal penning in a single player in action.
explanation.definitionFit: An ambition is an aim or target someone strives for, so it is a synonym of goal.

clue.text: Among Scots Mister Johnny Hallyday's the pinnacle of rock

parts.note: mister is a Scots word meaning need
Hallyday was a French rock star, and le is French for the

explanation.surface: Johnny Hallyday, the French rock legend, hailed as rock's summit even among Scots.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Mister' looks like a title but is a Scots verb and noun for need.
explanation.definitionFit: A needle is a sharp spire of rock, like the Needles off the Isle of Wight.

clue.text: Back to boat due to native impounding schooners

indicators.note: to impound is to shut something up, so one word encloses the other

parts.note: a son of a place is a native of it
a tern is a three-masted schooner

explanation.surface: Fishing schooners seized by locals and sent back to port.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Schooners' also suggests glasses of sherry; here they are ships.
explanation.definitionFit: A sternson is the timber at the back end of a ship joining the keelson to the sternpost.

clue.text: Tender name, possibly

indicators.note: possibly signals one possible arrangement among many, so the words are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A guess at what a pet name might be.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue is both definition and wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: A term of endearment like darling is an affectionate pet name, a tender one.

clue.text: Flipping fourth stock online message

indicators.note: flipping something over turns it end to end, so the letters run backwards

parts.note: D is the fourth letter of the alphabet
stock as in lineage or breed

explanation.surface: An irritated reaction to a fourth batch of shares sent by email.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Flipping' reads as a mild British exclamation, but it signals the turnaround.
explanation.definitionFit: An e-card is a greeting card sent over the internet, so an online message.

clue.text: In Tacitus by the way see developing porky

indicators.note: developing means changing form, so these letters take a new order

parts.note: OB abbreviates obiter, Latin for by the way, the language of Tacitus
this word's letters rearranged

explanation.surface: Reading the Roman historian, one notices someone putting on weight.
explanation.definitionFit: Porky is informal for fat, and obese means very overweight.

clue.text: Breaking finger isn't going to be the cause of whimpering

indicators.note: breaking something smashes it apart so the pieces can be rearranged

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written, apostrophe dropped

explanation.surface: A reassurance that a broken finger will not set anyone whimpering.
explanation.definitionFit: To snifter is a dialect verb for sniffing or snivelling, so sniftering is crying softly.

clue.text: Bear in mind dropping a penny could get you this dosh sorted

indicators.note: sorted means put into a different order, so the remaining letters are rearranged
dropping means letting go, so letters fall out of the phrase

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written
D is the symbol for an old British penny

explanation.surface: Advice that sorting your money and dropping a penny will see you right.
explanation.walkthrough: D, from Latin denarius, was the penny before decimal currency.
explanation.definitionFit: The renminbi is China's currency, and dosh is British slang for money.

clue.text: He ices a couple of out-of-date cakes on the spot

parts.note: cake is an old word for a fool, as is ass, so two of them
in, as in present at the place

explanation.surface: A baker piping icing on two stale cakes there and then.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Ices' is slang for kills, not decorating with icing.
explanation.definitionFit: To ice someone is slang for murdering them, so one who ices is a killer.

clue.text: We cut fresh sweet basil flowers

indicators.note: fresh means new, so the remaining letters form a new arrangement
to cut is to remove, so those two letters are excised from the herb phrase

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A gardener snipping fresh sweet basil and other blooms.
explanation.definitionFit: Astilbes are feathery-plumed garden perennials, flowers in the saxifrage family.

clue.text: After docking lively rating's rung

indicators.note: docking means cutting off the tail, so the final letter goes

parts.note: rattling as in brisk

explanation.surface: A sailor making a lively phone call once his ship is in port.
explanation.walkthrough: A rating is a non-commissioned sailor; 'rung' looks like a past tense but is a ladder step.
explanation.definitionFit: A rattlin (ratline) is one of the small ropes forming steps on a ship's shrouds, a sailor's ladder rung.

clue.text: To do with minister to special TA, say

parts.note: re means concerning
to minister to is to serve
S is an abbreviation for special

explanation.surface: A note about a minister dealing with a special Territorial Army matter.
explanation.walkthrough: The TA is the Territorial Army, Britain's volunteer reserve force.
explanation.definitionFit: The TA was the army's volunteer reserve, so it is an example of reserves, as the 'say' signals.

clue.text: Rab C's abuse is unexpected and quiet without pressure

indicators.note: without means lacking, so that letter must be left out

parts.note: snap as in a snap decision
a call for quiet
P is the symbol for pressure

explanation.surface: A Glasgow TV character's sudden outburst turning eerily quiet.
explanation.walkthrough: Rab C. Nesbitt is a Glaswegian TV comedy character, pointing to a Scots word.
explanation.definitionFit: Snash is Scots for insolent abuse or cheek, the kind of language Rab C would use.

clue.text: Government barristers freeing Baron's teens

parts.note: G abbreviates government

indicators.note: freeing means releasing, so that letter is let go from the lawyers' word

parts.note: a brief is slang for a barrister
B abbreviates baron

explanation.surface: Government lawyers getting a nobleman's teenage children released.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Teens' looks like adolescents, but teen is an old word for sorrow.
explanation.definitionFit: Teen is an archaic word for grief or affliction, so its plural matches the answer.

clue.text: Jump to a conclusion about lieutenant needling suspect

indicators.note: needling evokes a needle going into cloth, so the pair is pushed inside the outer word

parts.note: sus is slang for suspect
a is an old prefix meaning about, as in a-hunting
the standard abbreviation

explanation.surface: Accusing an officer of being shady without the evidence to back it up.
explanation.definitionFit: Saltus is Latin for a leap, used for a jump in reasoning or a break in continuity.

clue.text: Dear Father (as some have it) in a letter of Cavafy's

parts.note: lamb as a term of affection
da is a dialect word for dad

explanation.surface: A letter addressed to a priest, as written by the Greek poet Cavafy.
explanation.walkthrough: Cavafy was a modern Greek poet, so his letters are Greek ones.
explanation.definitionFit: Lambda is the eleventh letter of the Greek alphabet, the language Cavafy wrote in.

clue.text: Bingo's destiny — time together with love

parts.note: one's lot is one's fate
T abbreviates time
love is zero in tennis, which looks like O

explanation.surface: A bingo player's fate being romance in due course.
explanation.definitionFit: Lotto is a game of numbered cards much like bingo, and an alternative name for it.

clue.text: Find only child coming in after the expected time

indicators.note: coming in means entering, so the abbreviation goes inside the other word

parts.note: late means behind schedule
OC abbreviates only child

explanation.surface: Tracking down an only child who has arrived home late.
explanation.definitionFit: To locate something is to discover where it is, a synonym of find.

clue.text: Looked for wonder-struck papist denying odd points within

indicators.note: within means inside, so the kept letters go inside the reaction word

parts.note: awed means filled with wonder

indicators.note: denying the odd-numbered letters leaves only the even-numbered ones

parts.note: the second, fourth and sixth letters

explanation.surface: A Catholic in awe, gazing up at holy points of light.
explanation.walkthrough: The even letters split the reaction word after its first two letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Awaited means expected or watched out for, which is looking for something to come.

clue.text: Hostel in present poet's praise

indicators.note: in places the hostel letter inside the word for present

parts.note: here as in in attendance
Y, from YHA or YMCA, is a hostel

explanation.surface: A youth hostel singing the praises of a poet in residence.
explanation.walkthrough: Herye is a Spenserian word, hence 'poet's'.
explanation.definitionFit: Spenser used herye to mean praise or glorify, so it is a poetic word for praise.

clue.text: Barking's councillor beside the necessary beauties

parts.note: Cr is the abbreviation for councillor
the necessary is slang for money, as is ackers; beside just joins them

explanation.surface: A councillor in Barking, an East London borough, with funds and lovely companions.
explanation.walkthrough: Barking is a London district but means mad here; a cracker is also slang for a beauty.
explanation.definitionFit: Barking (short for barking mad) and crackers are both slang for insane; a cracker is also an attractive person.

clue.text: Old gossip's reach, no time in disappearing

indicators.note: disappearing means vanishing, so the short time word vanishes from the longer word

parts.note: to amount to is to reach a total
a mo is a moment, almost no time

explanation.surface: An elderly gossip's reach vanishing in no time at all.
explanation.definitionFit: In Shakespeare an aunt could mean an old woman or gossip, an archaic sense.

clue.text: Zeno's lecture arena is beside Academy

parts.note: is contracted to 's
to as in close to, as in a door pulled to
A abbreviates academy

explanation.surface: Where the philosopher Zeno taught, standing next to Plato's Academy.
explanation.walkthrough: Zeno of Citium taught in the Painted Porch at Athens, which gave the Stoics their name.
explanation.definitionFit: A stoa is a Greek colonnade, and the Stoa Poikile was where Zeno lectured.

clue.text: Old relation sinks back clutching what's still to be found

indicators.note: back means going the other way, so the word runs right to left
clutching means gripping, so the turned word holds the unknown inside

parts.note: ebbs means falls away
in algebra y is an unknown quantity

explanation.surface: An ancient relative sinking back while holding on to an undiscovered treasure.
explanation.definitionFit: Sybbe is an old spelling of sib, meaning a kinsman or relation.

clue.text: Force in Arabia, one term for spirit

indicators.note: in places the force symbol inside the regional abbreviation

parts.note: Ar abbreviates Arabia or Arabic
F is the symbol for force
Roman numeral one

indicators.note: a term is an end or limit, so only the closing letter is kept

parts.note: its final letter

explanation.surface: A powerful spirit at work in Arabia, as one word describes it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Spirit' does double duty: it is the definition and also gives its own last letter.
explanation.definitionFit: An afrit (ifrit) is a powerful evil demon of Arabian mythology.

clue.text: In offensive way during last month amiably dismissing leader

indicators.note: dismissing the leader sends away the first letter

parts.note: in as in during
December, the last month of the year
gently as in kindly

explanation.surface: Someone behaving offensively last month while pleasantly sacking the boss.
explanation.definitionFit: Indecently means in an improper or offensive manner, an adverb matching the phrase.

clue.text: Old hawks backing speech in Senate

indicators.note: backing means moving backwards, so the result reads right to left
in puts the word for speech inside the abbreviation

parts.note: Sen abbreviates senate
a say is one's chance to speak

explanation.surface: Veteran war hawks supporting a speech in the Senate.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Hawks' suggests political hardliners; here they are birds.
explanation.definitionFit: Nyas is an old falconry word, a variant of eyas, for a young hawk taken from the nest.

clue.text: Number to call, say, written alongside a muzhik's wagon

parts.note: tel abbreviates telephone number
e.g., for example
taken as written

explanation.surface: A phone number noted down beside a Russian peasant's cart.
explanation.walkthrough: A muzhik is a Russian peasant.
explanation.definitionFit: A telega is a rough four-wheeled Russian cart without springs, a peasant's vehicle.
